chapters.title: The Word of the Cross
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 1

Greeting

1Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

2to the church of God that is in Corinth, to those made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, together with all those who in every place call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

3grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Thanksgiving

4I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,

5that in every way you were made rich in Him, in all speech and all knowledge,

6just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,

7so that you are not lacking in any gift as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

8He will also keep you strong to the end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9God is faithful, by whom you were called into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

Divisions in the Church

10I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be knit together in the same mind and the same judgment.

11For it has been made clear to me by Chloe's people, my brothers, that there are quarrels among you.

12What I mean is this: each of you says, "I belong to Paul," or "I belong to Apollos," or "I belong to Cephas," or "I belong to Christ."

13Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

14I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

15so that no one can say that you were baptized in my name.

16I did baptize the household of Stephanas as well; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.

17For Christ did not send me to baptize but to preach the gospel, and not with wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ would not be emptied of its power.

The Foolishness of God

18For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

19For it is written:
"I will destroy the wisdom of the wise,
and the understanding of the understanding I will set aside."

20Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

21For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through its wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of what we preach to save those who believe.

22Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,

23but we preach Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

24but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

25For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

26Consider your calling, brothers: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth.

27But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;

28God chose what is low and despised in the world, the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are,

29so that no human being might boast before God.

30It is from Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and holiness and redemption,

31so that, as it is written, "Let him who boasts boast in the Lord."

Notes

  • vv17–18 "not with wisdom of words… the word of the cross is foolishness" — ouk en sophia logou… ho logos ho tou staurou: Paul refuses one kind of logos, wisdom made of words, and preaches another, the logos of the cross, the word of John 1:1. The cross is mōria, foolishness, to Greeks and skandalon, a stumbling block, to Jews (v23), the word of a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense (Romans 9:33).

  • vv19–20 "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise… Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe?" — Isaiah 29:14 in the Greek, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, where the Hebrew has the wisdom of their wise men will perish. Its last word in both is hidden; Paul has I will set aside. Where is the scribe? answers the Greek of Isaiah 33:18, Where are the scribes?, spoken over the fall of the Assyrian.

  • v28 "the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are" — ta mē onta, the words of Romans 4:17, the God who calls into being what does not exist. The God who calls what is not chooses what is not.

  • vv26–31 "not many wise… not many powerful… not many of noble birth… Let him who boasts boast in the Lord" — Jeremiah 9:23–24: Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom; let not the mighty man boast in his might; let not the rich man boast in his riches; but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me. Paul's three are Jeremiah's wise and mighty, with noble birth in place of riches, and the boast is still in the Lord, which in Paul's sentence follows straight on from Christ Jesus (v30).

chapters.title: The Wisdom of God in a Mystery
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 2

Christ Crucified

1When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with lofty speech or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony of God.

2For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.

3I came to you in weakness and in fear and with much trembling,

4and my speech and my preaching were not with the persuasion of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

5so that your faith would not rest on the wisdom of men but on the power of God.

The Hidden Wisdom

6Yet among the mature we do speak wisdom, though not a wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.

7We speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom that God appointed beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.

8None of the rulers of this age understood it, for if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

9But, as it is written:
"What no eye has seen and no ear has heard,
and what has not come into the heart of man,
what God has prepared for those who love Him" —

10these things God has revealed to us through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.

11For who knows a person's thoughts except the spirit of that person, which is in him? So also no one has known the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

12We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may understand what God has freely given us.

13These things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things in spiritual words.

14The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are judged spiritually.

15The spiritual person judges all things, but is himself judged by no one.

16"For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?" But we have the mind of Christ.

Notes

  • vv6–8 "the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing… they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" — hoi archontes tou aiōnos toutou can be the men who put Jesus to death, the high priests and Pilate, or the unseen powers behind them, as Romans 8:38 counts rulers, archai, among the powers that cannot separate us from the love of God. The Lord of glory is a title of God in 1 Enoch, the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the Eternal King (1 Enoch 25:3), and Psalm 24 calls Him the King of glory. Paul gives it to the one who was crucified.

  • v9 "What no eye has seen and no ear has heard" — as it is written, but no verse reads exactly so. The nearest is Isaiah 64:4, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for the one who waits for Him; what has not come into the heart is in the Greek of Isaiah 65:17. Paul has for those who love Him where Isaiah has for the one who waits for Him.

  • vv13–15 "spiritual things in spiritual words… The natural person… The spiritual person" — pneumatikois pneumatika synkrinontes can be read explaining spiritual things in spiritual words, to spiritual people, or comparing spiritual things with spiritual. Psychikos, natural, is from psychē, the life every human being has; pneumatikos, spiritual, from pneuma, the Spirit God gives. The same pair returns in 15:44, a natural body… a spiritual body.

  • v16 "who has known the mind of the Lord… But we have the mind of Christ" — Isaiah 40:13 in the Greek, which Paul quoted in Romans 11:34 to say no one has. Here he answers it: the mind of the Lord, YHWH in Isaiah, is given in the mind of Christ.

chapters.title: God's Field, God's Building
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 3

Still of the Flesh

1But I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as people of the flesh, as infants in Christ.

2I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able to take it. Even now you are not able,

3for you are still of the flesh. While there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not of the flesh, and living in a merely human way?

4For when one says, "I belong to Paul," and another, "I belong to Apollos," are you not merely human?

Servants of God

5What, then, is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you came to believe, as the Lord gave to each.

6I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.

7So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who gives the growth.

8The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive his own wages according to his own labor.

9For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, God's building.

The Foundation

10According to the grace of God given to me, like a skilled master builder I laid a foundation, and someone else is building on it. Let each one take care how he builds on it.

11For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

12If anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,

13each one's work will become plain, for the Day will show it, because it will be revealed by fire, and the fire itself will test what sort of work each one has done.

14If the work that anyone has built on the foundation survives, he will receive wages.

15If anyone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss, though he himself will be saved, but only as through fire.

God's Temple

16Do you not know that you are God's temple and that the Spirit of God lives in you?

17If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him. For God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.

All Things Are Yours

18Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, let him become a fool, so that he may become wise.

19For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, "He catches the wise in their own craftiness,"

20and again, "The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty."

21So let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

22whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future — all are yours,

23and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

Notes

  • vv10–11 "I laid a foundation… no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ" — Isaiah's foundation, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation (Isaiah 28:16), the stone Paul named in Romans 9:33. Paul laid it at Corinth; what others build on it, the fire of the Day will test.

  • vv16–17 "you are God's temple… you are that temple" — naos, the inner sanctuary where God dwelt, not the whole temple court. You is plural all through: the church together is where the Spirit of God lives. Phtheirei… phtherei, destroys… will destroy, is one verb, the punishment matching the deed.

  • vv19–20 "He catches the wise in their own craftiness… The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty" — Job 5:13, in words closer to the Hebrew than to the Greek, and Psalm 94:11, which reads the thoughts of man, that they are a breath: Paul has the wise where the psalm has man. Mataioi, empty, is the word of Romans 1:21, their thinking became empty.

  • vv21–23 "all are yours, and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's" — the slogans of 1:12 turned around. They said I am Paul's, I am Apollos'; Paul answers that Paul and Apollos belong to them, and they belong to no one but Christ.

chapters.title: Fools for Christ's Sake
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 4

Stewards of the Mysteries

1This is how people should reckon us: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

2What is required of stewards, moreover, is that each be found faithful.

3But to me it matters very little that I should be judged by you or by any human day of judgment. I do not even judge myself.

4For I know of nothing against myself, but I am not justified by that. The one who judges me is the Lord.

5So do not pronounce judgment before the time, before the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and make known the purposes of hearts, and then each one will receive his praise from God.

Nothing Beyond What Is Written

6I have applied all this to myself and Apollos for your sake, brothers, so that you may learn from us the saying "Nothing beyond what is written," and none of you may be puffed up in favor of one man against another.

7For who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? If you received it, why do you boast as if you had not?

8Already you have all you want! Already you have become rich! Without us you have become kings! I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you.

9For I think God has put us apostles on display last of all, like men sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men.

10We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are held in honor, but we in disgrace.

11To this very hour we go hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed and beaten and homeless,

12we labor, working with our own hands. When we are reviled, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure;

13when we are slandered, we answer kindly. We have become like the scum of the world, the refuse of all things, to this day.

My Beloved Children

14I do not write these things to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

15For though you may have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

16So I urge you, be imitators of me.

17That is why I sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, to remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, as I teach them everywhere in every church.

18Some of you have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

19But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of these puffed-up people but their power.

20For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

21Which do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

Notes

  • vv3–5 "any human day of judgment… I am not justified by that… then each one will receive his praise from God" — anthrōpinēs hēmeras, word for word a human day, set against the Day that the fire will reveal (3:13). A clear conscience does not acquit: dedikaiōmai, I am justified, the court verb of Romans, belongs to the Lord's verdict alone. His praise from God is the end of Romans 2:29, his praise is not from people but from God.

  • vv6, 18–19 "Nothing beyond what is written… puffed up" — four Greek words, mē hyper ha gegraptai, and the meaning has never been settled: keep within the Scriptures Paul has just quoted (1:19, 31; 3:19–20), or within what Scripture says at all. Physioō, puff up: six of its eight uses in the New Testament are in this letter, down to love is not puffed up (13:4).

  • vv12–13 "When we are reviled, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure" — the teaching of Jesus lived out: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you (Luke 6:28), which Paul had given the Romans as Bless those who persecute you (Romans 12:14).

chapters.title: Clean Out the Old Yeast
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 5

A Man and His Father's Wife

1It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind not found even among the Gentiles: a man has his father's wife.

2Yet you are puffed up! Should you not rather have mourned, so that the one who did this would be removed from among you?

3For though I am absent in body, I am present in spirit, and as if present I have already passed judgment on the one who did this.

4When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus, and my spirit is with you, with the power of our Lord Jesus,

5you are to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.

Christ Our Passover

6Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump of dough?

7Clean out the old yeast, so that you may be a new lump, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

8So let us keep the feast, not with the old yeast, the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

Judging Those Inside

9I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with the sexually immoral,

10not meaning the sexually immoral of this world at all, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would have to go out of the world.

11But now I am writing to you not to associate with anyone who goes by the name of brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy, or an idolater, a slanderer, a drunkard or a swindler — not even to eat with such a man.

12For what business is it of mine to judge those outside? Is it not those inside whom you are to judge?

13God judges those outside. "Purge the evil from among you."

Notes

  • v1 "a man has his father's wife" — the law of Leviticus 18:8, You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. Has, echein, is to live with a woman as one's own. Paul does not call her the man's mother.

  • v5 "hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved" — paradounai, the verb of God handed them over (Romans 1:24). The flesh can be the man's body, so that sickness or death follows, or the flesh as Romans uses it, the self that sins (Romans 8:13). The goal is rescue, not ruin: that his spirit may be saved.

  • vv6–8 "Clean out the old yeast… Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" — the first night of Passover, when Israel put away leaven from every house and ate unleavened bread seven days (Exodus 12:15), and Moses said slaughter the Passover (12:21). Paul reads the church as the house to be cleared, and Christ as the lamb already killed: the feast has begun.

  • v13 "Purge the evil from among you" — the refrain of Deuteronomy, So you shall purge the evil from among you (17:7; 22:21, and more), said there after the punishment of a grave sin in Israel. Paul gives the church the words Moses gave the people.

But now I am writing to you not to associate with anyone who goes by the name of brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy, or an idolater, a slanderer, a drunkard or a swindler — not even to eat with such a man.
For what business is it of mine to judge those outside? Is it not those inside whom you are to judge?
God judges those outside. "Purge the evil from among you."

chapters.title: Bought with a Price
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 6

Lawsuits Among Believers

1When one of you has a dispute with another, does he dare to go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints?

2Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? If the world is to be judged by you, are you not fit to try the smallest cases?

3Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more, matters of this life!

4So if you have such cases, why do you seat as judges those who count for nothing in the church?

5I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to settle a dispute between brothers,

6but brother goes to law against brother, and that before unbelievers?

7To have lawsuits with one another at all is already a defeat for you. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?

8Instead, you yourselves do wrong and cheat, and your own brothers at that!

Washed, Made Holy, Justified

9Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate men, nor men who lie with men,

10nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.

11Such were some of you. But you were washed, you were made holy, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.

Your Body Is a Temple

12"All things are lawful for me" — but not all things are good for me. "All things are lawful for me" — but I will not be mastered by anything.

13"Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food" — and God will do away with both one and the other. The body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

14God raised the Lord, and He will raise us up too, by His power.

15Do you not know that your bodies are parts of Christ? Shall I then take the parts of Christ and make them parts of a prostitute? By no means!

16Or do you not know that whoever is joined to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For it is said, "The two will become one flesh."

17But whoever is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with Him.

18Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.

19Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,

20for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "the saints will judge the world… we will judge angels" — Daniel's vision, judgment was given to the holy ones of the Most High, and… the holy ones possessed the kingdom (Daniel 7:22). Angels under judgment are the story of 1 Enoch, where the angels who sinned are bound until the day of their judgment (1 Enoch 10:12) and Enoch tells Azazel A great judgment has gone out against you (13:1). Paul does not say which angels.

  • v4 "why do you seat as judges those who count for nothing in the church?" — kathizete can be a question, a rebuke for taking cases before outsiders the church does not esteem, or a command, seat as judges even those who count for least in the church: better the least of the believers than the courts of unbelievers.

  • v9 "effeminate men, nor men who lie with men" — malakoi, word for word soft ones, the word of soft clothing in Jesus' question about John (Matthew 11:8). In this list it stands beside the next word, and whether it means effeminate men in general or the passive partner in sex between men is not settled. Arsenokoitai is made of the two words of the Greek of Leviticus 20:13, meta arsenos koitēn, lying with a male: A man who lies with a male as one lies with a woman.

  • vv16–17 "The two will become one flesh… whoever is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with Him" — Genesis 2:24, clings to his woman, and they become one flesh, in the words Jesus used (Mark 10:8). Kollōmenos, joined, is the Greek of clings in Genesis, and Paul uses it both of the man joined to a prostitute and of the one joined to the Lord.

  • vv19–20 "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit… you were bought with a price" — in 3:16 the temple was the church together; here it is each one's own body. Ēgorasthēte, you were bought, from agora, the market. Paul says it again in 7:23, You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.

chapters.title: Married and Unmarried
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 7

Husbands and Wives

1Now about the things you wrote: "It is good for a man not to touch a woman."

2But because of the temptation to sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.

3The husband should give his wife what is due her, and likewise the wife her husband.

4The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

5Do not deprive one another, unless perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may give yourselves to prayer; then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

6I say this as a concession, not as a command.

7I wish that everyone were as I am. But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another.

8To the unmarried and the widows I say: it is good for them to remain as I am.

9But if they cannot control themselves, they should marry, for it is better to marry than to burn with passion.

The Lord's Command

10To the married I give this command — not I, but the Lord: the wife should not separate from her husband

11(but if she does separate, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband), and the husband should not divorce his wife.

12To the rest I say — I, not the Lord: if any brother has a wife who is an unbeliever, and she is willing to live with him, he should not divorce her.

13If any woman has a husband who is an unbeliever, and he is willing to live with her, she should not divorce her husband.

14For the unbelieving husband is made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy through her husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy.

15But if the unbeliever separates, let him separate. In such cases the brother or the sister is not bound. God has called you to peace.

16For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

Remain as You Were Called

17Only, let each one live the life the Lord has assigned him, as God has called him. This is what I direct in all the churches.

18Was anyone called when he was already circumcised? He should not undo his circumcision. Was anyone called when uncircumcised? He should not be circumcised.

19Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; keeping the commandments of God is what counts.

20Each one should remain in the condition in which he was called.

21Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it trouble you; but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.

22For the one who was called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord's freedman; likewise the one who was free when called is Christ's slave.

23You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.

24Brothers, each one should remain before God in the condition in which he was called.

The Unmarried

25Now about virgins: I have no command from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who by the Lord's mercy is trustworthy.

26I think, then, that because of the present distress it is good for a person to remain as he is.

27Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

28But if you do marry, you have not sinned, and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet those who marry will have troubles in this life, and I would spare you that.

29What I mean, brothers, is this: the time has been cut short. From now on, those who have wives should live as though they had none,

30those who weep as though they were not weeping, those who rejoice as though they were not rejoicing, those who buy as though they had no goods,

31and those who use the world as though they had no full use of it. For the present form of this world is passing away.

32I want you to be free from worry. The unmarried man is concerned about the things of the Lord, how to please the Lord.

33But the married man is concerned about the things of the world, how to please his wife,

34and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the things of the Lord, so as to be holy in body and in spirit; but the married woman is concerned about the things of the world, how to please her husband.

35I say this for your own good, not to put a noose on you, but to promote what is fitting and to help you serve the Lord without distraction.

Giving a Daughter in Marriage

36If anyone thinks he is not acting properly toward his virgin daughter, if she is past the bloom of youth and it must be so, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning. Let them marry.

37But whoever stands firm in his heart, being under no necessity but having control over his own will, and has decided in his heart to keep his virgin daughter, will do well.

38So the one who gives his virgin daughter in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage will do better.

Widows

39A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives. But if her husband falls asleep, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord.

40Yet in my judgment she is happier if she remains as she is, and I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

Notes

  • v1 "It is good for a man not to touch a woman" — peri de hōn egrapsate, about the things you wrote: Paul is answering a letter from Corinth. The line that follows can be a saying from that letter, which Paul quotes and then qualifies (But… each man should have his own wife), as he quoted All things are lawful for me in 6:12; or it can be his own view, which the rest of the chapter limits. The Greek has no quotation marks.

  • vv10–12 "not I, but the Lord… I, not the Lord" — Paul sets the words of Jesus apart from his own. The wife should not separate, chōristhēnai, is the verb of Jesus' saying, What God has joined together, let no man separate (Mark 10:9); for the case Jesus did not address, a believer married to an unbeliever, Paul speaks on his own authority. He does it again in v25, I have no command from the Lord.

  • v21 "if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity" — mallon chrēsai, word for word rather use it, with no object. It can be the freedom just named, take the opportunity, or the slave's present calling, make the most of it instead, in keeping with each one should remain (vv20, 24). V23, do not become slaves of men, leans toward freedom.

  • vv29–31 "the time has been cut short… the present form of this world is passing away" — synestalmenos, cut short, drawn in. Schēma, form, is the outward shape of a thing, the word Paul uses of Christ found in form as a man (Philippians 2:7). Marriage, grief, joy, buying and selling stay, but they are held loosely, because the world in its present shape will not last.

  • vv36–38 "his virgin daughter… the one who gives his virgin daughter in marriage" — the Greek says only his virgin. Gamizōn, giving in marriage, is the verb of neither marry nor are given in marriage (Matthew 22:30), always so in the Gospels, and points to a father deciding about his unmarried daughter. Many English Bibles read instead a man and the young woman he is engaged to, with gamizō taken as marry. Hyperakmos, past the bloom, can be said of her age or of strong desire.

chapters.title: Food Offered to Idols
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 8

Knowledge and Love

1Now about food offered to idols: we know that "we all have knowledge." Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

2If anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know as he ought to know.

3But if anyone loves God, he is known by Him.

One God and One Lord

4So, about eating food offered to idols: we know that "an idol is nothing in the world," and that "there is no God but one."

5For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as indeed there are many gods and many lords,

6yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.

Do Not Make Your Brother Stumble

7But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, being used to idols until now, still eat the food as offered to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

8Food will not bring us near to God. We are no better off if we eat, and no worse off if we do not.

9But take care that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.

10For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, weak as it is, be built up to eat food offered to idols?

11So by your knowledge this weak man is destroyed, the brother for whom Christ died.

12When you sin against your brothers in this way and wound their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.

13Therefore, if food makes my brother stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not make my brother stumble.

Notes

  • vv1, 10 "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up… be built up to eat food offered to idols" — physioi… oikodomei: knowledge swells a man like air; love builds like a house, the building of 3:9. In v10 Paul turns the word on the knowing: the weak brother is built up, oikodomēthēsetai, all right, built up to eat what his conscience forbids.

  • vv4–6 "there is no God but one… one God, the Father, from whom are all things… and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things" — the Shema, Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), in its Greek words theos and kyrios, God and Lord. Paul keeps Israel's confession that God is one and sets the two words of it side by side: one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things are from the Father and through the Lord.

  • vv11–13 "the brother for whom Christ died… you sin against Christ" — the words of Romans 14:15, Do not, by what you eat, destroy the one for whom Christ died. To wound a brother is to sin against Christ, as the risen Jesus asked Saul, why are you persecuting Me? (Acts 9:4).

chapters.title: All Things to All People
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 9

The Rights of an Apostle

1Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

2If to others I am not an apostle, at least I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

3This is my defense to those who would examine me.

4Do we not have the right to eat and drink?

5Do we not have the right to take a believing wife along with us, as the other apostles do, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?

6Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to stop working for a living?

7Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat any of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink any of the milk?

8Am I saying this only on human authority? Does not the Law say the same?

9For it is written in the Law of Moses, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing." Is it for oxen that God is concerned?

10Or is He not speaking entirely for our sake? It was written for our sake, because the one who plows should plow in hope, and the one who threshes should thresh in hope of a share in the crop.

11If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?

12If others share this right over you, do not we even more? But we have not made use of this right; instead we put up with anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.

13Do you not know that those who serve in the temple eat from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar?

14In the same way, the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living from the gospel.

My Wages

15But I have made use of none of these things, and I am not writing this so that it will be done for me. I would rather die than — no one will empty my boast!

16For if I preach the gospel, that gives me no ground for boasting, because necessity is laid on me. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!

17If I do this of my own will, I have wages; if not of my own will, I am still entrusted with a stewardship.

18What then are my wages? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.

All Things to All People

19For though I am free from all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I might win more of them.

20To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win Jews. To those under the Law I became like one under the Law, though I myself am not under the Law, to win those under the Law.

21To those outside the Law I became like one outside the Law, though I am not outside the law of God but within the law of Christ, to win those outside the Law.

22To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all means I might save some.

23I do it all for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in it with them.

Run So as to Win

24Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to win it.

25Every athlete exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a wreath that withers, but we a wreath that never withers.

26So I do not run aimlessly; I do not box as one beating the air.

27No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after preaching to others I myself will not be disqualified.

Notes

  • vv9–10 "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing. Is it for oxen that God is concerned?" — Deuteronomy 25:4, a law about animals set among laws about people. Paul reads it as written for our sake: if the ox may eat from the grain it treads, the worker may live from his work. He does the same with Abraham in Romans 4:23–24, not written for his sake alone, but for ours also.

  • v14 "the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living from the gospel" — a saying of Jesus, the worker deserves his wages (Luke 10:7), given when He sent out the seventy-two. Paul keeps the right and gives it up: his wages are to preach for nothing (v18).

  • vv20–21 "under the Law… outside the Law… not outside the law of God but within the law of Christ" — anomos, outside the Law, ennomos, within the law: three words from the one root. Paul is free of the Law of Moses as the line between Jew and Gentile, but not lawless: he is bound to Christ, and through Christ to God.

  • vv24–27 "only one receives the prize… a wreath that withers… I discipline my body" — the games: the runner, the boxer, the victor's stephanos, a wreath of leaves. Hypōpiazō, word for word I strike under the eye, a boxer's blow, the word of the judge who fears the widow will wear me out (Luke 18:5); adokimos, disqualified, the word of the worthless mind that failed the test (Romans 1:28).

chapters.title: The Rock Was Christ
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 10

Patterns for Us

1For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,

2and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

3and all ate the same spiritual food,

4and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

5Yet with most of them God was not pleased, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

6These things took place as patterns for us, so that we would not desire evil as they did.

7Do not be idolaters, as some of them were; as it is written, "The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play."

8We must not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day.

9We must not put Christ to the test, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the serpents.

10Do not grumble, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

11These things happened to them as a pattern, and they were written down for our instruction, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

12So let anyone who thinks he stands take care that he does not fall.

13No testing has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and He will not let you be tested beyond what you can bear; with the testing He will also provide the way out, so that you can endure it.

The Table of the Lord

14Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

15I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.

16The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?

17Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

18Look at the people of Israel: are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?

19What do I mean, then? That food offered to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?

20No, but that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to be sharers with demons.

21You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

22Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He is?

Do All to the Glory of God

23"All things are lawful," but not all things are good for us. "All things are lawful," but not all things build up.

24Let no one seek his own good, but the good of the other.

25Eat whatever is sold in the meat market without raising any question for the sake of conscience,

26for "the earth is the Lord's, and all that fills it."

27If one of the unbelievers invites you to dinner and you want to go, eat whatever is set before you without raising any question for the sake of conscience.

28But if someone says to you, "This has been offered in sacrifice," do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience —

29I mean not your own conscience but the other person's. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?

30If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced over what I give thanks for?

31So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

32Give no offense to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God,

33just as I try to please everyone in everything, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

Notes

  • vv1–4, 9 "the cloud… the sea… the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ… We must not put Christ to the test" — the Exodus read as the church's own story: the cloud and the sea as a baptism, the manna and the water as spiritual food and drink. The water came from a rock at the start of the wandering (You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, Exodus 17:6) and again near its end (Numbers 20:11); Moses' song calls God Himself The Rock (Deuteronomy 32:4, 15). Paul names the rock Christ, and says Israel tested Christ in the wilderness (v9; Numbers 21:6).

  • vv6–11 "patterns for us… twenty-three thousand fell in a single day… destroyed by the destroyer" — typoi, patterns, the word of Adam as a pattern of the one who was to come (Romans 5:14). V7 is the golden calf (Exodus 32:6); v8 is Baal of Peor, where Numbers 25:9, in the Hebrew and the Greek, counts twenty-four thousand who died in the plague. The destroyer is the one the LORD would not let enter your houses to strike on the night of Passover (Exodus 12:23).

  • vv16–17 "a sharing in the blood of Christ… one bread, one body" — koinōnia, sharing, the word of fellowship with His Son (1:9). The many who eat the one loaf are made one body: the meal itself is the argument against eating at the table of idols.

  • vv20, 22 "they sacrifice to demons and not to God… are we provoking the Lord to jealousy?" — Moses' song again, They sacrificed to demons, not God (Deuteronomy 32:17), in the Greek word for word as Paul has it, and They made Me jealous with what is no god (32:21), the verse Paul used in Romans 10:19 and 11:11. The song that told Israel's idolatry tells the Corinthians'.

chapters.title: The Lord's Supper
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 11

1Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.

Covered and Uncovered Heads

2I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold to the traditions just as I handed them on to you.

3But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.

4Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head,

5but every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, since it is one and the same as if her head were shaved.

6For if a woman will not cover her head, she might as well cut off her hair; but if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, she should cover her head.

7A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

8For man was not made from woman, but woman from man.

9Neither was man created for the woman, but woman for the man.

10That is why a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.

11Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man of woman.

12For as woman came from man, so man comes through woman; and all things come from God.

13Judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

14Does not nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it is a disgrace to him,

15but if a woman has long hair it is her glory? For her hair is given to her as a covering.

16If anyone is inclined to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.

Divisions at the Lord's Supper

17But in giving these instructions I do not praise you, because when you come together it is not for the better but for the worse.

18For, to begin with, I hear that when you come together as a church there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.

19There must indeed be factions among you, so that those who are approved may be recognized among you.

20When you come together, then, it is not the Lord's supper that you eat.

21For in eating, each one goes ahead with his own supper; one goes hungry and another gets drunk.

22What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.

The Night He Was Handed Over

23For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was handed over, took bread,

24and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, "This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me."

25In the same way He took the cup after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."

26For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes.

27So whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy way will be guilty of sinning against the body and the blood of the Lord.

28Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup.

29For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.

30That is why many of you are weak and ill, and a number of you have fallen asleep.

31But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would not be judged.

32When we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.

33So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

34If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that when you come together it will not be for judgment. The other matters I will set in order when I come.

Notes

  • vv3–7, 15 "the head of every man is Christ… dishonors his head… her hair is given to her as a covering" — kephalē, head, is both the head on the body and the one to whom a person is joined, and Paul uses both at once: a man who covers his own head dishonors his head, Christ. Whether head here means authority over or source of is debated; vv8 and 12, woman from man… man through woman, speak of source. The covering may be a veil or the hair itself, as v15 says. The image and glory of God is Genesis 1:27, and woman from man is the woman built from the man's side (Genesis 2:22).

  • v10 "authority over her head, because of the angels" — exousian echein epi tēs kephalēs, word for word to have authority on her head, which can be her own authority, her right to pray and prophesy (v5), or a sign that she is under authority, as many English Bibles add. Because of the angels has never been settled: the angels present when the church worships, or the angels of Genesis 6, the sons of God saw the daughters of humankind (Genesis 6:2), told at length in 1 Enoch, The angels, the sons of heaven, saw them and desired them (1 Enoch 6:2).

  • vv23–25 "on the night when He was handed over… This is My body, which is for you… This cup is the new covenant in My blood" — the words of Luke 22:19–20, nearly word for word. Paredideto, was handed over, is Judas's betrayal and also God's own giving, He… handed Him over for us all (Romans 8:32); Paul handed on what he received, with the same verb. The new covenant is Jeremiah's, I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel (Jeremiah 31:31), sealed in blood as the first was, Here is the blood of the covenant (Exodus 24:8).

  • v29 "without discerning the body" — the body can be the Lord's body given in the bread, or the church, which Paul has just called one body (10:17): the rich who eat first and leave the poor hungry (vv21–22) fail to see the body they are part of.

chapters.title: One Body, Many Parts
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 12

The Same Spirit

1Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be unaware.

2You know that when you were Gentiles you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.

3So I want you to understand that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed!" and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.

4There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit;

5there are different kinds of service, but the same Lord;

6there are different kinds of working, but the same God, who works all of them in everyone.

7To each one is given the showing of the Spirit for the common good.

8To one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge by the same Spirit,

9to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit,

10to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the ability to tell spirits apart, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

11All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who gives to each one individually as He wills.

One Body

12For just as the body is one and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.

13For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, Jews or Greeks, slaves or free, and all were given one Spirit to drink.

14For the body does not consist of one part but of many.

15If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body.

16If the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body.

17If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole body were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?

18But as it is, God has arranged the parts in the body, each one of them, as He chose.

19If all were a single part, where would the body be?

20As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

21The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."

22On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

23and the parts of the body we think less honorable we treat with greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty,

24which our presentable parts do not need. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,

25so that there would be no division in the body, but the parts would have the same care for one another.

26If one part suffers, all the parts suffer with it; if one part is honored, all the parts rejoice with it.

27Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a part of it.

28God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, guiding, and various kinds of tongues.

29Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?

30Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

31But earnestly desire the greater gifts. Yet I will show you a still more excellent way.

Notes

  • vv4–6 "the same Spirit… the same Lord… the same God" — three lines built alike, each ending on one of the three: the Spirit who gives the gifts, the Lord who is served, God who works them all. Paul has just said no one can call Jesus… Lord except by the Spirit (v3), the confession of Romans 10:9.

  • vv12–13, 27 "so it is with Christ… you are the body of Christ" — Paul does not say so it is with the church, but so it is with Christ: the many members are His body. In Romans 12:4–5 the same picture taught that no one should think too highly of himself; here it teaches the proud that they need the weak, and the weak that they belong.

  • v31 "earnestly desire the greater gifts" — zēloute can be a command, earnestly desire, or a statement, you are eager for the greater gifts, Paul describing what the Corinthians are already doing before he shows them a still more excellent way. 14:1 has the same verb as a command, earnestly desire the spiritual gifts.
